currentContext.business: Established in 1995, Aditya Infotech designs, manufactures, markets and distributes a broad portfolio of video surveillance and electronic security products under the CP PLUS brand, spanning IP and analogue cameras, network video recorders, AI-enabled and specialised cameras, and surveillance-aligned accessories. The Company is primarily engaged in the trading and distribution of these products, while manufacturing is undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh. It serves government, enterprise, commercial, industrial and residential customers across India through a channel-led model of distributors, dealers, system integrators and exclusive retail stores.

Professional Range: Specialised cameras such as explosion-proof and global shutter

related.name: AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited
related.note: Wholly owned subsidiary. Originally incorporated on February 8, 2017 as a 50:50 joint venture between the Company and Dixon Technologies (India) Limited to manufacture and market security and surveillance products including DVRs, CCTV cameras, alarm systems, electrical appliances, energy devices, gadgets and related components. After nearly eight years as a JV, the Company acquired the entire shareholding of its JV partner and made it a wholly owned subsidiary with effect from September 18, 2024. Operates the manufacturing facility at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh engaged in manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, trading and servicing of security and surveillance products including CCTV cameras, DVRs, cables, software and related accessories.

related.name: Shenzhen CP Plus International Ltd.

related.name: Aditya Infotech Taiwan Co. Ltd
related.note: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on February 2, 2026 under the laws of Taiwan, newly formed during FY 2025-26. Established primarily to undertake research and development activities in security and surveillance technologies, strengthening the Company's global presence and R&D capabilities.

related.name: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited
related.note: Former 50% joint venture partner in AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited until the Company acquired its entire shareholding effective September 18, 2024. currentContext.expansion: Aditya Infotech is running a two-track expansion: adding manufacturing capacity and simultaneously pulling components in-house through backward integration. Manufacturing sits with wholly owned subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh, where a capacity augmentation plan taken up during FY 2025-26 raises installed capacity from 24 million to 30 million CCTV and surveillance products per annum by adding 6 million units of annual capacity. On backward integration, Phase-1 of a state-of-the-art in-house housing and enclosures plant is scheduled to become operational by Q3 FY2027 with Phase-2 following in Q4 FY2027, targeting a peak production capacity of 30 million housings and enclosures per annum (elsewhere in the report management describes Phase-1 as live by Q2 FY27 and the MD's message puts the Kadapa enclosures and housing facility at Q3 FY27). A new lens assembly line is being introduced at the Kadapa facility with an initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million lenses per month; the CCTV camera lens assembly line was commissioned during the year with commercial production targeted from FY27, and the report elsewhere describes an initial 3 lakh lenses per month scaling to 10 lakh per month by the end of the following year. Component localisation also runs through a strategic joint venture with Orient Cables to manufacture high-grade LAN and CCTV cables, networking cables and camera and recorder cables, for which a dedicated 1 lakh sq. ft. facility is being set up in Rajasthan with commercial production slated to commence between Q2 and Q3 of FY2027. Management anticipates that full operational efficiency and EBITDA margin expansion from these initiatives will materialise sequentially through FY2028, and aims to localise over 50% of Bill of Materials cost as the cable joint ventures and housing plants go live sequentially through FY2027. On physical footprint, the Kadapa facility has been upgraded with an additional 50,000 sq. ft. manufacturing shed with further land acquisition proposals underway, active evaluations are ongoing for land acquisitions in Northern India, and an upcoming 3 lakh sq. ft. facility in Sector 68, Noida is targeted to be operational by Q4 FY27. Together with Kadapa land-bank additions, this supports a 2X capacity roadmap to double the current manufacturing milestone of 2.5 million units from existing levels by FY2028, matched to expanding order pipelines from large-scale smart cities, infrastructure projects, NHAI and Indian Railways. For operational flexibility, mature HD analog job work is planned to move to external EMS partners, adding flexible capacity of 0.5 million units per month and keeping internal high-value assets at 90% to 100% utilisation while they focus on high-margin, complex AIoT integrations. R&D capacity is expanding in parallel: DSIR-approved in-house laboratories anchor a research footprint across Noida, Ahmedabad and Taiwan with a team of over 200 engineers and specialists, reinforced R&D centres in Noida and Ahmedabad, and a new specialised tech centre being established in Bangalore. Under a definitive agreement with L&T Semiconductor Technologies, the Company is co-developing India's first indigenous IP Systems-on-Chips with advanced Vision AI, a chipset framework planned to power 9 million CP PLUS cameras over the next three years.

risks.note: Unpredictable market conditions, inflation, political instability and shifting government policies may impact business sentiment and consumer spending, thereby affecting revenue growth. Demand for surveillance hardware is discretionary at the residential and commercial end and geared to infrastructure and government spending cycles.

Geopolitical instability, supply shocks, natural disasters, pandemics and other logistical constraints may disrupt the flow of goods, leading to delays in production, shipping and distribution. The Company's manufacturing depends on imported components routed through international freight lanes.

risks.risk: Global semiconductor and critical component scarcity
risks.note: Critical components including SoCs, DDR, flash memory and advanced sensors remained under persistent supply pressure from manufacturing constraints and supply-demand imbalances, causing extended manufacturing lead times. Mitigated through a multi-SoC product architecture and a diversified multi-supply-chain procurement framework that eliminates single-source dependency.

risks.risk: Geopolitical volatility and escalating supply chain costs
risks.note: Sustained geopolitical instability in the Middle East introduced acute operational pressures, causing sharp inflation in global insurance premiums and ocean freight costs. Mitigated by fast-tracking the infrastructure roadmap - the localised housing and enclosure plant and the scalable lens assembly line at Kadapa - to insulate cost structures from international freight volatility.

Intense competition can lead to pricing pressures, reduced market share and margin compression, requiring continuous innovation to maintain customer relevance and counter emerging market entrants. The report notes unorganised players entering the structural vacuum created by the exit of non-compliant brands.

The competitive reset the Company is benefiting from is regulation-driven - STQC certification requirements, BIS standards and government advisories on trusted sources for surveillance systems. Continued compliance with these evolving certification and procurement regimes is a condition of market access.

Given the nature of surveillance products, the Company must maintain system integrity, data localisation and secure data handling, and align with the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Cybersecurity oversight has been delegated by the Board to the Risk Management Committee.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the expansion and backward-integration roadmap
risks.note: Forward-looking plans across housing and enclosures, lens assembly, cable joint ventures, new facilities and indigenous SoC development carry the risk that actual results differ materially from expectations; the Company's own cautionary statement flags regulatory change, ability to implement strategies, growth and expansion, technological change and market-risk exposure as sources of divergence.

thesis: Clear market leader in India's organized video surveillance industry. Own-brand CP PLUS share jumped from ~25% (pre-STQC) to ~45.4% by Q3 FY26 (mgmt cited "close to 46%"), vastly exceeding the IPO-time target of ~36%, as the STQC mandate forced Chinese players out and consolidated share to Indian manufacturers. CP PLUS = 86% of AIL revenue; IP products = 73% of CP PLUS portfolio (premiumization/mix-up ongoing). FY27 guidance raised to ~50% revenue growth. Key tension: semiconductor/memory (SoC, DDR3, flash, sensors) global shortage is pushing input costs up through 2027 — company is passing on via gradual monthly price hikes, so PAT growth may lag revenue growth.
scorecard (reported; yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 (full year) | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 1,422 cr | +45.5% | INR 4,220.8 cr | +35.6% | Demand across retail/project/govt; market-share gains |
| EBITDA | INR 258.3 cr | +162% | INR 579 cr | +124.1% | Mix + localization + opex efficiency |
| EBITDA margin | 18.0% | +800 bps | 13.7% | +540 bps | Q4 margin flagged as one-off (low-cost inventory + Q4 price hike + project-SKU mix) |
| Gross margin | ~31.8% (Q4) | +~900 bps | n/a | — | Mix (more IP), Q4 price rise, low-cost inventory now exhausted |
| Adjusted PAT | INR 169.1 cr | +207.7% | INR 368 cr | +166.1% | Finance cost down 38% (Q4) / 27.8% (FY) post IPO debt repayment |

**One-offs / quality flags:** Q4 gross/EBITDA margin boosted by (a) low-cost inventory now fully exhausted — replacement inventory at higher cost, (b) Jan-2026 price hike of 6–8%, (c) project/high-end SKU mix coming in H2 post-STQC certification. Mgmt explicitly: Q4 18% margin is a one-off; sustainable normal is 14–15%. PAT is "Adjusted PAT" (normalization basis not detailed in transcript).
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 revenue: INR 6,000–6,500 cr** (raised from earlier guidance) ≈ ~50% growth over FY26.
- **FY27 EBITDA margin: 14–15%** (called the "new normal" for FY27 & FY28; up from earlier 12–13% view).
- **FY27 PAT: ~8.5–9.5%** of revenue.
- **Volume growth FY27: 25–30%** (vs industry units +15–16%); **ASP/per-unit recovery +20–25%** (mix + price, not purely price).
- **Price hikes:** 6–8% taken Jan-2026; ongoing gradual monthly single-digit-bps hikes through FY27; cost escalation expected until 2027.
- **Capex FY27: INR 200–300 cr** (raised from ~INR 200 cr); funded by internal accruals + some debt for plant & machinery.
- **Localization mix:** backward integration (housing, cables, lens, SoC) full benefits in FY28; capacity to 2x existing by FY28; complete backward integration targeted by FY28.
demand / pipeline:
- Industry units to grow ~15–16% (mgmt brought down its own assumption from >20% to ~15% factoring ASP-led demand moderation). B2B is the core — consumer/home <10% of business, so less exposed to entry-level price-elasticity (unlike mobiles/laptops).
- Pent-up demand from FY25 (muted due to STQC transition) expected to flow into FY27; commercial/project/enterprise still strong.
- Government ~15–20% of revenue (tenders via SIs/PSUs); "no rockstar" expectation — steady.
- Entry-level IP cameras/recorders see higher % cost rise → possible shift to HD analog at low end; enterprise/project less affected.
segment:
- CP PLUS brand = 86% of AIL revenue; IP = 73% of CP PLUS portfolio (rising).
- Verticals: home/consumer, SMB, enterprise/project, government — mgmt claims it is the only brand relevant across ALL segments.
- New multi-brand strategy: **Nexivue** (certified, shipping since Apr-2026) and **Eyra** (R&D rework due to supply chain; STQC cert ~2 months out, to market next quarter) — positioned at different price points to defend/expand share.
growth / optionality:
- **In-house mfg / backward integration:** housing (in-house plant, 50 machines; target 30M housings/yr — Phase-1 Q2FY27, Phase-2 Q4FY27); CCTV lens production at Kadapa (5 lakh/mo scalable to 1M/mo); coaxial/Cat6 cable localization + Orient Cables JV (Rajasthan, ~1 lakh sq ft, ops Q2–Q3 FY27); LTSCT indigenous vision-SoC (9M IP cameras/3yrs). Capacity now 2.5M units; target 90–100% utilization; doubling by FY28.
- **IoT / AI:** Qualcomm partnership for AI-enabled video security (in trials, phased commercial rollout); cameras evolving "viewing → recording → analytics → AI decision-making."
- **Service / recurring revenue (new optionality):** cloud backup (home market, becoming mass-market) + AI-as-a-Service / SaaS security model (Qualcomm-driven) — margin accretive but "too early," 5-yr payoff.
- **Exports / ODM-OEM:** focus area but deprioritized vs domestic for now; may "kick-off some action this year"; people approaching for OEM but SoC reserved for own demand.
- HD analog job-work to be moved to EMS players (~0.5M units/month, scalable).
margins & cost:
- New normal EBITDA margin 14–15% (up from prior 12–13% view) driven by localization, premiumization, enterprise mix, brand mix, opex efficiency.
- Headwind: semiconductor/memory shortage (DDR3 lines shifted to DDR5 for AI), high USD, Middle-East freight/insurance — input cost up to 2027. Low-cost inventory exhausted.
- Mitigation: multi-SoC (6 non-Chinese suppliers), multi-supply-chain sourcing (fabs, distributors, open market), forward procurement, gradual price pass-through. Time lag means profitability growth may trail revenue.
capex: - FY27 INR 200–300 cr (internal accruals + some debt). Includes housing plant, lens line, Kadapa additional land + 50,000 sq ft shed, Noida Sector-68 3 lakh sq ft facility (operational Q4FY27), R&D centres (Noida, Ahmedabad, new Bangalore, Taiwan office/R&D). Evaluating further land in North India. FY28 capex plans still being worked out (likely higher).
capital allocation:
- IPO proceeds used to repay debt → finance cost down 27.8% (FY) / 38% (Q4); minimal debt-equity ratio.
- Priorities: capex + selective EPS-accretive inorganic/M&A; R&D investment.
- Dividend declared: INR 1.6 per share (face value INR 1).
- Working-capital / cash-conversion cycle inched up (advance payments + lower creditor days to secure chips/memory) — flagged as deliberate, factored into FY27 WC planning.
risks:
- **China / component dependence:** despite "non-Chinese" SoC strategy, global semiconductor & memory shortage (SoC, DDR3, flash, sensors) is the dominant risk; contracts "going haywire," force-majeure invalidations; costs rising weekly/fortnightly through 2027.
- **Margin/price-pass-through lag:** profitability may not mirror revenue; demand elasticity at entry-level IP from ASP hikes.
- **Competition:** Hikvision/Dahua (Chinese) share collapsed post-STQC; ~30 certified brands (≈12 global ≈10% share; ~18 domestic, mostly ≤1/10th of CP PLUS size). Peer certification picking up — potential FY28+ threat; mgmt claims wide moat (brand, scale mfg, R&D, full-segment range, supply-chain head-start).
- Forex (high USD), Middle-East geopolitics (freight/insurance), working-capital stretch.
management tone: Highly confident/bullish — "stellar numbers," raised guidance, "defining year." Candid on margin one-off (won't repeat Q4 18%), candid on supply-chain being "unprecedented in 2-3 decades." Measured on exports and SaaS ("too early"). Credible, detailed on operational specifics.
non-obvious:
- Half of 6–7 large non-Chinese DDR makers stopped DDR3 (shifted to DDR5 for AI data centers) — surveillance-grade memory squeeze; "big get bigger, small tail most affected" — shortage is a competitive moat for the leader.
- Q4 margin flatters trailing optics; the real run-rate is 14–15%, materially above the prior 12–13% market view — re-rating of structural margin.
- SaaS/cloud + AI-edge is a future recurring-revenue optionality not yet in numbers (5-yr horizon).
- Taiwan R&D + global 20-yr-experience talent hire signals up-the-stack ambition (own SoC/vision via LTSCT).
challenges → beneficiaries:
- China+1 / STQC import-substitution beneficiary: ✅ CP PLUS (CPPLUS) itself — primary beneficiary of surveillance localization.
- Indigenous semiconductor push: ⭐ L&T Semiconductor Technologies (LTSCT), Orient Cables (cable JV) as ecosystem participants.
- AI-edge surveillance: Qualcomm partnership (platform supplier).
- (Listed-peer beneficiary list left for aggregation — no direct listed Indian competitor named beyond the company itself.)

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aditya Infotech Limited, through its flagship brand CP PLUS, is India's leading Indian-owned video surveillance and electronic security solutions provider and the country's first and only listed pure-play surveillance company.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1995, Aditya Infotech designs, manufactures, markets and distributes a broad portfolio of video surveillance and electronic security products under the CP PLUS brand, spanning IP and analogue cameras, network video recorders, AI-enabled and specialised cameras, and surveillance-aligned accessories. The Company is primarily engaged in the trading and distribution of these products, while manufacturing is undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh. It serves government, enterprise, commercial, industrial and residential customers across India through a channel-led model of distributors, dealers, system integrators and exclusive retail stores.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary. Originally incorporated on February 8, 2017 as a 50:50 joint venture between the Company and Dixon Technologies (India) Limited to manufacture and market security and surveillance products including DVRs, CCTV cameras, alarm systems, electrical appliances, energy devices, gadgets and related components. After nearly eight years as a JV, the Company acquired the entire shareholding of its JV partner and made it a wholly owned subsidiary with effect from September 18, 2024. Operates the manufacturing facility at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh engaged in manufacturing, assembling, importing, exporting, trading and servicing of security and surveillance products including CCTV cameras, DVRs, cables, software and related accessories.
- Shenzhen CP Plus International Ltd. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on December 30, 2016 under the laws of the People's Republic of China. Provides procurement support and operational assistance in sourcing raw materials, spare parts, components and finished goods, and undertakes quality assurance including product testing, inspection, quality control and technical evaluation of products sourced from international markets.
- Aditya Infotech Taiwan Co. Ltd — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on February 2, 2026 under the laws of Taiwan, newly formed during FY 2025-26. Established primarily to undertake research and development activities in security and surveillance technologies, strengthening the Company's global presence and R&D capabilities.
- Dixon Technologies (India) Limited — related party: Former 50% joint venture partner in AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited until the Company acquired its entire shareholding effective September 18, 2024. Held board nomination rights under Article 102A of the Articles of Association, which ceased effective May 25, 2026, triggering the resignation of its nominee Mr. Atul B. Lall from the Board.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains a highly attractive high-growth market within the global CCTV ecosystem, with rising investment in public infrastructure, smart urban development, enterprise security and residential protection broadening adoption across user segments
- The STQC framework is reinforcing higher cybersecurity standards and encouraging adoption of compliant products; management indicated at the time of the IPO that STQC implementation could support a meaningful increase in the market share of domestic brands, and remains encouraged by the structural shifts underway
- Exclusion of non-compliant players and the gradual exit of Chinese brands has created a structural vacuum, shifting demand towards compliant domestic brands, with Indian manufacturers now commanding the majority of the market and unorganised players expected to consolidate as Indian capacity comes on stream
- Increasing awareness of product quality, cybersecurity and regulatory compliance is contributing to a more structured and organised market environment
- The Indian video surveillance and security market, valued at $4.40 billion in 2025, is expected to grow at a 16-17% CAGR; Frost & Sullivan places India's revenue CAGR for FY25-30 at 16.46% and volume CAGR at 13.50%, the fastest among major regions
- The global video surveillance market, valued at US$35.9 billion in Fiscal 2025, is expected to expand at a 10.36% CAGR between Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2030
- Industry mix shift: hardware accounted for over 62% of the market in 2025 while VSaaS is the fastest-growing segment at an 11.19% CAGR, and IP-based solutions comprise nearly 55% of deployments - supporting the Company's IP and AI-led positioning
- Government programmes - Smart Cities Mission, Digital India, smart policing, Make in India, the INR 22,919 crore electronic-components PLI scheme, EMC 2.0 and the India Semiconductor Mission - are expanding demand and strengthening the domestic manufacturing ecosystem
- Mandatory CCTV requirements in banks, ATM centres and educational institutions, plus declining IP camera costs, are accelerating the analogue-to-IP transition
- Headwind: supply-demand imbalances, geopolitical uncertainty and manufacturing constraints keep key components - System-on-Chip, DDR, flash and sensors - under periodic supply pressure
- Headwind: elevated freight and insurance costs and currency volatility have increased procurement complexity across the value chain
- Macro backdrop: India delivered 7.7% GDP growth in FY2025-26 and is projected to grow 6.6% in FY2026-27, the fastest among major economies, with the FY2026-27 Union Budget allocating Rs 12.22 lakh crore to capital expenditure, an 11.5% increase

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aditya Infotech is running a two-track expansion: adding manufacturing capacity and simultaneously pulling components in-house through backward integration. Manufacturing sits with wholly owned subsidiary AIL Dixon Technologies Private Limited at Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh, where a capacity augmentation plan taken up during FY 2025-26 raises installed capacity from 24 million to 30 million CCTV and surveillance products per annum by adding 6 million units of annual capacity. On backward integration, Phase-1 of a state-of-the-art in-house housing and enclosures plant is scheduled to become operational by Q3 FY2027 with Phase-2 following in Q4 FY2027, targeting a peak production capacity of 30 million housings and enclosures per annum (elsewhere in the report management describes Phase-1 as live by Q2 FY27 and the MD's message puts the Kadapa enclosures and housing facility at Q3 FY27). A new lens assembly line is being introduced at the Kadapa facility with an initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million lenses per month; the CCTV camera lens assembly line was commissioned during the year with commercial production targeted from FY27, and the report elsewhere describes an initial 3 lakh lenses per month scaling to 10 lakh per month by the end of the following year. Component localisation also runs through a strategic joint venture with Orient Cables to manufacture high-grade LAN and CCTV cables, networking cables and camera and recorder cables, for which a dedicated 1 lakh sq. ft. facility is being set up in Rajasthan with commercial production slated to commence between Q2 and Q3 of FY2027. Management anticipates that full operational efficiency and EBITDA margin expansion from these initiatives will materialise sequentially through FY2028, and aims to localise over 50% of Bill of Materials cost as the cable joint ventures and housing plants go live sequentially through FY2027. On physical footprint, the Kadapa facility has been upgraded with an additional 50,000 sq. ft. manufacturing shed with further land acquisition proposals underway, active evaluations are ongoing for land acquisitions in Northern India, and an upcoming 3 lakh sq. ft. facility in Sector 68, Noida is targeted to be operational by Q4 FY27. Together with Kadapa land-bank additions, this supports a 2X capacity roadmap to double the current manufacturing milestone of 2.5 million units from existing levels by FY2028, matched to expanding order pipelines from large-scale smart cities, infrastructure projects, NHAI and Indian Railways. For operational flexibility, mature HD analog job work is planned to move to external EMS partners, adding flexible capacity of 0.5 million units per month and keeping internal high-value assets at 90% to 100% utilisation while they focus on high-margin, complex AIoT integrations. R&D capacity is expanding in parallel: DSIR-approved in-house laboratories anchor a research footprint across Noida, Ahmedabad and Taiwan with a team of over 200 engineers and specialists, reinforced R&D centres in Noida and Ahmedabad, and a new specialised tech centre being established in Bangalore. Under a definitive agreement with L&T Semiconductor Technologies, the Company is co-developing India's first indigenous IP Systems-on-Chips with advanced Vision AI, a chipset framework planned to power 9 million CP PLUS cameras over the next three years.
